messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty page fired for service="inference-prod" incident=PDR-98231 escalation_policy="platform-oncall" — triggered by alert: "high error rate /model/serve". Auto-created at 2026-03-14T02:35:01Z
PagerDutyBot: Triggered details: 60 errors/min over 5m, region=us-west-2, source=prometheus-alertmanager. Routing key used: rk_abc123.
Sarah Kim: whoa — that escalation policy looks wrong. inference-prod should go to "inference-oncall" not platform. pinging oncall.
Mike Lopez: I see the same in PD UI. There's a duplicate service binding referencing a legacy schedule `platform-night` that shouldn't exist. Checking audit logs.
Ashley Nguyen: @Sarah Kim @Mike Lopez I got the page on my phone. Can confirm it's going to platform-oncall, not the inference roster. I'm going to ack to stop noisy pages and triage.
eng-oncall: acked PDR-98231. Taking ownership for now. :hand:
Raj Patel: thanks. Mike, can you re-route? If we change routing key we can reassign to correct service without a customer-facing escalation.
Mike Lopez: copying the PD API call I'm using to reassign the service mapping: ```bash
curl -X PUT "https://api.pagerduty.com/services/SV123" \
  -H "Authorization: Token token=$PD_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": {"escalation_policy": {"id": "EP_INFERENCE_ONCALL"}}}'
```
Mike Lopez: applied the update at 2026-03-14T02:39:12Z. Confirmed service `inference-prod` now points to EP_INFERENCE_ONCALL.
PagerDutyBot: Escalation policy change recorded in audit. Previous policy=EP_PLATFORM_ONCALL by user `automation-sync` at 2026-03-14T01:12:07Z.
Sarah Kim: what caused automation-sync to bind inference-prod to platform? sounds like a sync job bug. Any idea?
Mike Lopez: looking at the sync job logs. There's a schedule overlap check that failed when a legacy schedule `platform-night` had a shadow tag `inference`. Sync interpreted tag and assigned wrong policy. Log snippet: ```json
{"job":"schedule-sync","service":"inference-prod","match_tag":"inference","action":"assign","meta":"legacy-tagged"}
```
Raj Patel: customer impact? Did any customers get 5xx or long tail latency while pages were firing?
eng-oncall: We saw elevated 5xxs starting ~02:33Z for ~11 minutes. Traffic analysis: ~0.8% of requests hit the failing shard that lost autoscale due to misrouted oncall, fallback didn't trigger immediately. We moved traffic to read-only fallback at 02:36Z which reduced errors.
Ashley Nguyen: FYI I pushed a hotfix to the fallback router at 02:37Z to force-model-fallback for heavy requests. That brought error rate down to baseline by 02:44Z.
Sarah Kim: good. Can we make a temporary PD rule to suppress duplicate pages while we fix the sync? We were getting duplicate pages to platform and inference at the same time.
Mike Lopez: created a temporary suppress rule in PD (scope: inference-prod, duration: 30m) at 02:40Z. Also revoked legacy schedule binding from `automation-sync` job config to prevent immediate re-sync.
PagerDutyBot: Suppression rule created by Mike.Lopez.
Raj Patel: action items for follow-up: 1) fix schedule-sync tag matching logic (owner: infra/scheduling) 2) add integration test that simulates legacy-tagged services (owner: eng-ml) 3) postmortem with timeline and customer impact (owner: oncall lead) 4) verify no other services have shadow tag collisions (owner: platform team).
Sarah Kim: I'll own the postmortem write-up. Mike, Raj — can you draft the code patch and review? Putting a follow-up meeting at 1600 PT.
eng-oncall: Incident closed in PD at 02:50Z after manual verification. Final note: customer-facing SEV avoided; some customers reported transient errors, no data loss.
Ashley Nguyen: adding labels: root_cause=legacy-schedule-shadow, mitigation=manual-reassign+fallback, followup=code-fix+tests.
Mike Lopez: pushing PR with fix for tag matching: https://git.internal/redwood/schedule-sync/pull/432 : please review.
Sarah Kim: :thumbsup: thanks everyone. I'll start the timeline and share draft in #postmortems later today.
